s:
With reference to the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme, consider the following statements:
1. It was revamped as DILRMP from 1 April 2016.
2. It was converted into a Central Sector Scheme with 100% central funding.
3. The Department of Land Resources under the Ministry of Rural Development is associated with its implementation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. DILRMP was revamped from 1 April 2016, became fully centrally funded, and is handled by the Department of Land Resources under the Ministry of Rural Development.
tq: Check the date, funding pattern and administrative department together before selecting the coded combination.
sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

s: The tenure of DILRMP was extended up to which period, along with which two new components?
o: 2025-26; consent-based Aadhaar seeding of land records and computerisation of revenue courts
x: The programme was extended from 2021-22 to 2025-26. Consent-based Aadhaar seeding of land records and computerisation of revenue courts were added as new components.
tq: Pair the extension period with the two newly added components.
sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

s: Which one of the following is NOT a core component of DILRMP?
o: Modern record rooms at tehsil level
Digitisation of cadastral maps and FMBs
Universal digitisation of agricultural subsidy beneficiary accounts
x: Modern record rooms, survey or resurvey, data entry, cadastral-map digitisation, State data centres, computerised registration and core GIS are DILRMP components. Universal digitisation of agricultural subsidy beneficiary accounts is not listed as a core component.
tq: Find the option that belongs to a neighbouring policy area rather than land-record modernisation.
sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

s: Which of the following correctly describes the mandatory gender-related provision in the Record of Rights under DILRMP?
o: A separate gender-based land tax is recorded in the Record of Rights.
Only the gender of the registering officer is entered.
A mandatory gender column is included in the Record of Rights.
Gender details are excluded from digitised land records.
x: DILRMP provides for a mandatory gender column in the Record of Rights.
tq: Look for the precise record-level provision rather than an administrative or taxation alternative.
sec: DILRMP - predecessors, funding, components

s:

x: NAKSHA is an urban pilot under DILRMP implemented through the Survey of India. It covers more than 150 cities, has an allocation of ₹194 crore and issues the ‘Ur Pro Card’.

s: ULPIN, also known as Bhu-Aadhaar, refers to:
o: A 16-digit code issued only for agricultural loans
A 14-digit registration number based on the village population
A 12-digit numeric code based on the owner’s Aadhaar number
A 14-digit alphanumeric identification number generated from the geo-coordinates of a parcel’s vertices
x: ULPIN means Unique Land Parcel Identification Number, or Bhu-Aadhaar. It is a 14-digit alphanumeric ID derived from the geo-coordinates of a parcel’s vertices.
tq: Distinguish the parcel-based geo-coordinate identifier from personal Aadhaar and registration numbers.

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the presumptive and conclusive systems of land titling?
o: Under the presumptive system the State guarantees title, whereas under the conclusive system title may be challenged through earlier deeds.
Under the presumptive system registration records a transaction, whereas under the conclusive system the State guarantees the title once issued.
Both systems rely on separate registration, survey and revenue records with no authoritative title register.
Neither system permits disputes regarding title after mutation is recorded.
x: In the presumptive system, registration records a transaction and title may be challenged through earlier deeds, mutation or possession. In the conclusive system, the State guarantees the title once it is issued.
tq: Reverse the two systems mentally and compare who bears the guarantee and whether title remains challengeable.
sec: Conclusive land titling - presumptive vs conclusive, Model Act

s: Which institutional arrangement characterises the conclusive land-titling system?
o: Registration, survey and revenue records are maintained separately.
A single authoritative title register is maintained.
Title is determined exclusively by possession records.
Only mutation records are maintained without registration records.
x: The conclusive system provides for a single authoritative title register, unlike the separate records maintained under the presumptive system.
tq: Use the record-structure distinction to separate the two titling models.
sec: Conclusive land titling - presumptive vs conclusive, Model Act

s:
Consider the following statements about the NITI Aayog Model Conclusive Land Titling Act, 2020:
1. It is a model framework.
2. Its adoption by States is compulsory.
3. It seeks to reduce disputes, facilitate credit and lower transaction costs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Act is a model framework and its objectives include fewer disputes, easier credit and lower transaction costs. Adoption is a matter of State choice, not compulsory.
tq: Spot the compulsory-adoption trap in an otherwise correct description of the model Act.
sec: Conclusive land titling - presumptive vs conclusive, Model Act

s: The Supreme Court decision of 1 January 2026 concerning registration and title held that:
o: A transfer deed cannot be registered unless a nationwide survey has been completed.
Registration of a transfer deed is distinct from title, and mandatory proof of mutation under the Bihar rule was not upheld.
Mutation is always superior to a registered transfer deed.
Registration of a transfer deed by itself conclusively establishes title in every case.
x: The Supreme Court held that registration of a transfer deed is distinct from title and did not uphold the Bihar requirement of mandatory proof of mutation. The judgment noted that land had not been surveyed nationwide since 1950.
tq: Focus on the legal distinction between registration, mutation and title rather than treating them as identical.
sec: Conclusive land titling - presumptive vs conclusive, Model Act
